name: storefront-tour
description: Twelve hand-authored natural-language questions over the bundled storefront package, written to vary grain, join depth, filter shape and answerability. Two ask for a business convention the model does not encode, two are deliberately open, and one has a silent wrong answer a careless grouping produces. Every case is `dev`: the set is a walkthrough meant to be run whole, so nothing is withheld from diagnosis. There is no holdout, so it cannot defend an acceptance check on a model edit without being re-split first.
sourceNote: Authored directly as a markdown numbered list in as-received/questions.md; one case per list item, question text copied byte for byte. No goldens arrived with them: every key here is derived by the conductor, first as DuckDB SQL over the raw parquet and then as Malloy through the truth package, and promoted only where the two agree.
auditNote: verify_goldens.py reports that dimension:customers:signup_date and products.retail_price do not appear in the model TEXT. Both are real and both are retrievable: they are columns the source exposes implicitly from the parquet, which a grep over the .malloy cannot see. Do not 'fix' those ids. check_findable.py returns 23 of 23 retrievable -- but only once the embedding index is ready. Run it against a server that has just started and it reports misses that are the lexical matcher, not the key; it now warns when it could not wait for the index.
